summary: Concrete MaterialDNA resilience gap: the contract says recipe validation/freezing is bounded, but malformed plain input can still force work and error growth proportional to attacker-controlled table size before the declared small-shape/list caps reject it. validateKnownFields scans every supplied key and appends one error per unknown key; validateDenseArray scans the entire supplied table before checking count > MAX_HISTORY_EVENTS/MAX_ANOMALY_MODIFIERS. Add a narrow source-only validation-work fence that short-circuits closed-record validation on the first unknown key and dense-array validation once invalid shape or maximum+1 entries is observed, with adversarial regressions proving oversized hostile records/lists reject without traversing the full payload.
evidence: Docs/MATERIAL_DNA_CONTRACT.md states recipe validation/freezing is bounded generation/persistence work and specifically cites the 32 history-event and 8 anomaly-modifier caps.

src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateKnownFields currently iterates every key in an arbitrary plain record and appends an error for every unknown key, so a malformed closed-shape record has no validation-work/error-count bound.

src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateDenseArray currently counts/scans the entire supplied table and only checks count > maximum after traversal; a huge dense historyEvents/anomalyModifiers table therefore defeats the intended small-list work bound before rejection.

Current materialdna_contract and materialdna_metatable_boundary suites cover shape, metatable/no-execute, sparse/keyed lists, hostile keys, and fixture-content seals, but do not assert bounded traversal/work on oversized malformed containers.

Active HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-COUNTERS / PR #313 is limited to maintenance.repairCount safe-integer exactness; prior evt-20260811-081620-mat8c3r1-materialdna-key-grammar is limited to percent-sign key grammar. This finding is non-overlapping.
